sanskrit: āvṛttis tatra caikasya nāsty āvṛttir manīṣiṇām ubhau tau devayānena gacchato jājale pathā
english: For one kind there is return to rebirth, but for the wise there is no returning; both these, O Jājali, travel by the path of the gods.

sanskrit: svayaṃ caiṣām anaḍuho yujyanti ca vahanti ca svayam usrāś ca duhyante manaḥsaṃkalpasiddhibhiḥ
english: For such men the oxen yoke and draw of their own accord, and the cows give milk of themselves, by the mere fulfilment of their mind's resolve.

sanskrit: svayaṃ yūpān upādāya yajante svāptadakṣiṇaiḥ yas tathābhāvitātmā syāt sa gām ālabdhum arhati
english: Of themselves they take up the sacrificial posts and worship with their own well-earned offerings; he whose self is so refined is worthy to lay hold of a cow for sacrifice.

sanskrit: oṣadhībhis tathā brahman yajeraṃs te natādṛśāḥ buddhityāgaṃ puraskṛtya tādṛśaṃ prabravīmi te
english: But men not of that stature, O brāhmaṇa, should sacrifice with herbs and plants alone; setting the renunciation born of wisdom foremost, such is the path I declare to you.

sanskrit: nirāśiṣam anārambhaṃ nirnamaskāram astutim akṣīṇaṃ kṣīṇakarmāṇaṃ taṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ
english: Free of craving, undertaking nothing, offering no obeisance and no praise, undiminished yet spent of all works — him the gods know as the true brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: nāśrāvayan na ca yajan na dadad brāhmaṇeṣu ca grāmyāṃ vṛttiṃ lipsamānaḥ kāṃ gatiṃ yāti jājale idaṃ tu daivataṃ kṛtvā yathā yajñam avāpnuyāt
english: Neither reciting the scriptures aloud, nor sacrificing, nor giving among brāhmaṇas, yet seeking a worldly livelihood — to what goal does such a man come, O Jājali? Tell me how, making this his deity, he may attain the fruit of sacrifice.

sanskrit: jājalir uvāca na vai munīnāṃ śṛṇumaḥ sma tattvaṃ; pṛcchāmi tvā vāṇija kaṣṭam etat pūrve pūrve cāsya nāvekṣamāṇā; nātaḥ paraṃ tam ṛṣayaḥ sthāpayanti
english: Jājali said: We have not heard the very truth of the sages; I ask you, O merchant — this is a hard matter. Not heeding what went ever before, the seers set down no doctrine higher than this.

sanskrit: asminn evātmatīrthe na paśavaḥ prāpnuyuḥ sukham atha svakarmaṇā kena vāṇija prāpnuyāt sukham śaṃsa me tan mahāprājña bhṛśaṃ vai śraddadhāmi te
english: In this holy ford of the self the beasts could not find their happiness; then by which deed of his own, O merchant, may a man attain happiness? Tell me this, O greatly wise one — deeply indeed do I trust your word.

sanskrit: tulādhāra uvāca uta yajñā utāyajñā makhaṃ nārhanti te kva cit ājyena payasā dadhnā pūrṇāhutyā viśeṣataḥ vālaiḥ śṛṅgeṇa pādena saṃbhavaty eva gaurmakham
english: Tulādhāra said: Whether they offer sacrifices or none, those rites are nowhere worthy of the true offering. With clarified butter, with milk and curds, above all with the full oblation — yes, by her hair, her horn, her hoof, the cow herself brings the sacrifice to be.

sanskrit: patnīṃ cānena vidhinā prakaroti niyojayan puroḍāśo hi sarveṣāṃ paśūnāṃ medhya ucyate
english: And by this rule a man appoints his wife to her office and so performs it; for the sacrificial cake is declared the pure oblation that stands for all the beasts.

sanskrit: sarvā nadyaḥ sarasvatyaḥ sarve puṇyāḥ śiloccayāḥ jājale tīrtham ātmaiva mā sma deśātithir bhava
english: All rivers are as the Sarasvatī, all mountains holy; the self alone, O Jājali, is the sacred ford — do not be a stranger wandering from land to land.

sanskrit: etān īdṛśakān dharmān ācarann iha jājale kāraṇair dharmam anvicchan na lokān āpnute śubhān
english: Practising such duties as these in this world, O Jājali, while seeking righteousness through outward means, a man does not attain the blessed realms.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca etān īdṛśakān dharmāṃs tulādhāraḥ praśaṃsati upapattyā hi saṃpannān nityaṃ sadbhir niṣevitān
english: Bhīṣma said: Such duties as these does Tulādhāra extol — duties accomplished by sound reasoning and ever followed by the good.

sanskrit: tulādhāra uvāca sadbhir vā yadi vāsadbhir ayaṃ panthāḥ samāśritaḥ pratyakṣaṃ kriyatāṃ sādhu tato jñāsyasi tad yathā
english: Tulādhāra said: Whether by the good or by the wicked this path has been resorted to, let it be made plain before your eyes, and then you shall know how the matter truly stands.

sanskrit: ete śakuntā bahavaḥ samantād vicaranti hi tavottamāṅge saṃbhūtāḥ śyenāś cānyāś ca jātayaḥ
english: These many birds wander all about you — hawks and creatures of other kinds, hatched and reared upon your very head.

sanskrit: āhvayainān mahābrahman viśamānāṃs tatas tataḥ paśyemān hastapādeṣu śliṣṭān dehe ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Call to them, O great brāhmaṇa, as they settle here and there; behold them clinging to your hands and feet and over all your body.

sanskrit: saṃbhāvayanti pitaraṃ tvayā saṃbhāvitāḥ khagāḥ asaṃśayaṃ pitā ca tvaṃ putrān āhvaya jājale
english: The birds, cherished by you, honour you as their father; beyond doubt you are their father — call to your children, O Jājali.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tato jājalinā tena samāhūtāḥ patatriṇaḥ vācam uccārayan divyāṃ dharmasya vacanāt kila
english: Bhīṣma said: Then, summoned by that Jājali, the winged ones uttered divine speech, speaking, so it is said, the word of dharma.

sanskrit: ahiṃsādikṛtaṃ karma iha caiva paratra ca spardhā nihanti vai brahman sāhatā hanti taṃ naram
english: The work founded upon non-injury and the rest bears fruit both here and beyond; but rivalry destroys it, O brāhmaṇa, and that rivalry, once roused, destroys the man himself.

sanskrit: śraddhāvṛddhaṃ vāṅmanasī na yajñas trātum arhati atra gāthā brahmagītāḥ kīrtayanti purāvidaḥ
english: Sacrifice cannot save the speech and mind that grow only through faith; here those versed in old lore recite the verses sung by Brahmā.

sanskrit: śucer aśraddadhānasya śraddadhānasya cāśuceḥ devāś cittam amanyanta sadṛśaṃ yajñakarmaṇi
english: The mind of the pure man without faith and of the impure man possessed of faith — the gods deemed these alike in the work of sacrifice.

sanskrit: śrotriyasya kadaryasya vadānyasya ca vārdhuṣeḥ mīmāṃsitvobhayaṃ devāḥ samam annam akalpayan
english: Of the learned but stingy man and of the generous usurer the gods weighed both, and reckoned their food as of equal worth.

sanskrit: prajāpatis tān uvāca viṣamaṃ kṛtam ity uta śraddhāpūtaṃ vadānyasya hatam aśraddhayetarat bhojyam annaṃ vadānyasya kadaryasya na vārdhuṣeḥ
english: Prajāpati said to them: This judgement is unequal. The generous man's food is hallowed by faith; the other's is spoiled by faithlessness. The generous man's food may be eaten, but not the stingy man's, nor the usurer's.

sanskrit: aśraddadhāna evaiko devānāṃ nārhate haviḥ tasyaivānnaṃ na bhoktavyam iti dharmavido viduḥ
english: He alone who lacks faith is unworthy of the gods' oblation; his food, and his alone, is not to be eaten — so know those learned in dharma.

sanskrit: aśraddhā paramaṃ pāpaṃ śraddhā pāpapramocanī jahāti pāpaṃ śraddhāvān sarpo jīrṇām iva tvacam
english: Faithlessness is the highest sin; faith is the deliverer from sin. The man of faith casts off his sin as a serpent its worn-out skin.

sanskrit: jyāyasī yā pavitrāṇāṃ nivṛttiḥ śraddhayā saha nivṛttaśīladoṣo yaḥ śraddhāvān pūta eva saḥ
english: Greatest among purifying things is renunciation joined with faith; he who has turned away from the faults of conduct and holds fast to faith is verily pure.

sanskrit: kiṃ tasya tapasā kāryaṃ kiṃ vṛttena kim ātmanā śraddhāmayo 'yaṃ puruṣo yo yacchraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ
english: What need has such a one of austerity, of observance, of any further discipline of self? This man is made of faith; whatever his faith is, that very thing is he.

sanskrit: iti dharmaḥ samākhyātaḥ sadbhir dharmārthadarśibhiḥ vayaṃ jijñāsamānās tvā saṃprāptā dharmadarśanāt
english: Thus has dharma been declared by the good who perceive its meaning and aim; we, desiring knowledge, have come to you out of our vision of dharma.

sanskrit: spardhāṃ jahi mahāprājña tataḥ prāpsyasi yat param śraddhāvāñ śraddadhānaś ca dharmāṃś caiveha vāṇijaḥ svavartmani sthitaś caiva garīyān eṣa jājale
english: Cast off rivalry, O greatly wise one, and then you shall attain the highest. Faithful and full of faith, fixed in his own path of duty, this merchant here is the worthier man, O Jājali.

sanskrit: evaṃ bahumatārthaṃ ca tulādhāreṇa bhāṣitam samyak caivam upālabdho dharmaś coktaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: Thus was the matter of high import set forth by Tulādhāra, and rightly was the eternal dharma grasped and declared.

sanskrit: tasya vikhyātavīryasya śrutvā vākyāni sa dvijaḥ tulādhārasya kaunteya śāntim evānvapadyata
english: Having heard the words of that Tulādhāra of renowned power, the twice-born one, O son of Kuntī, won his way to peace.

sanskrit: tato 'cireṇa kālena tulādhāraḥ sa eva ca divaṃ gatvā mahāprājñau viharetāṃ yathāsukham svaṃ svaṃ sthānam upāgamya svakarmaphalanirjitam
english: Then before long that Tulādhāra and he, both greatly wise, having gone to heaven, dwelt there in ease, each attaining his own station won by the fruit of his deeds.

sanskrit: samānāṃ śraddadhānānāṃ saṃyatānāṃ sucetasām kurvatāṃ yajña ity eva na yajño jātu neṣyate
english: For those who are even-minded, faithful, restrained, and pure of heart, when they perform what is called sacrifice, the sacrifice is never found wanting.

sanskrit: śraddhā vai sāttvikī devī sūryasya duhitā nṛpa sāvitrī prasavitrī ca jīvaviśvāsinī tathā
english: Faith indeed is the goddess of the quality of goodness, daughter of Sūrya, O king — Sāvitrī, the bringer-forth, and the giver of trust to all living things.

sanskrit: vāgvṛddhaṃ trāyate śraddhā manovṛddhaṃ ca bhārata yathaupamyopadeśena kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotum icchasi
english: Faith preserves what is grown through speech and grown through mind, O Bhārata. This has been taught you by way of parable — what more do you wish to hear?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam prajānām anukampārthaṃ gītaṃ rājñā vicakhnunā
english: Bhīṣma said: On this point too they tell this ancient tale, sung by King Vicakhnu out of compassion for living creatures.

sanskrit: chinnasthūṇaṃ vṛṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā virāvaṃ ca gavāṃ bhṛśam gograhe yajñavāṭasya prekṣamāṇaḥ sa pārthivaḥ
english: Seeing a bull with its post struck down and hearing the loud bellowing of the cattle at the cow-pen of the sacrificial ground, that king looked on.

sanskrit: svasti gobhyo 'stu lokeṣu tato nirvacanaṃ kṛtam hiṃsāyāṃ hi pravṛttāyām āśīr eṣānukalpitā
english: "May it be well with the cattle in all the worlds!" — thus he made his pronouncement; for once slaughter had begun, this blessing was devised.

sanskrit: avyavasthitamaryādair vimūḍhair nāstikair naraiḥ saṃśayātmabhir avyaktair hiṃsā samanukīrtitā
english: It was by men of no fixed bounds, deluded, denying the scriptures, of doubting and unsettled mind, that the killing of beasts came to be praised.

sanskrit: sarvakarmasv ahiṃsā hi dharmātmā manur abravīt kāmarāgād vihiṃsanti bahir vedyāṃ paśūn narāḥ
english: In all works non-injury is the law — so spoke Manu whose very self was righteousness; it is from lust and passion that men slaughter beasts outside the altar.

sanskrit: tasmāt pramāṇataḥ kāryo dharmaḥ sūkṣmo vijānatā ahiṃsaiva hi sarvebhyo dharmebhyo jyāyasī matā
english: Therefore the subtle dharma should be discharged by the discerning man according to right measure; for non-injury is held greater than all other duties.

sanskrit: upoṣya saṃśito bhūtvā hitvā vedakṛtāḥ śrutīḥ ācāra ity anācārāḥ kṛpaṇāḥ phalahetavaḥ
english: Having fasted and become rigorous in vows, yet abandoning the revealed truths the Veda ordains — calling it 'observance,' these are no observances at all, but the wretched practices of men set on reward.

sanskrit: yadi yajñāṃś ca vṛkṣāṃś ca yūpāṃś coddiśya mānavāḥ vṛthā māṃsāni khādanti naiṣa dharmaḥ praśasyate
english: If men, on the pretext of sacrifices, of sacred trees, and of sacrificial posts, eat flesh in vain, this is no dharma to be commended.

sanskrit: māṃsaṃ madhu surā matsyā āsavaṃ kṛsaraudanam dhūrtaiḥ pravartitaṃ hy etan naitad vedeṣu kalpitam
english: Flesh, honey, liquor, fish, strong drink, and rice cooked with sesame — all this was set going by cheats; it is nowhere ordained in the Vedas.

sanskrit: kāmān mohāc ca lobhāc ca laulyam etat pravartitam viṣṇum evābhijānanti sarvayajñeṣu brāhmaṇāḥ pāyasaiḥ sumanobhiś ca tasyāpi yajanaṃ smṛtam
english: Out of lust, delusion, and greed was this craving set in motion; in all sacrifices the brāhmaṇas recognize Viṣṇu alone, and his worship is held to be with milk-rice and with flowers.

sanskrit: yajñiyāś caiva ye vṛkṣā vedeṣu parikalpitāḥ yac cāpi kiṃ cit kartavyam anyac cokṣaiḥ susaṃskṛtam mahāsattvaiḥ śuddhabhāvaiḥ sarvaṃ devārham eva tat
english: And the trees fit for sacrifice that are appointed in the Vedas, and whatever else is to be done, when well prepared in purity by the great-souled and pure of heart — all that is worthy of the gods.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śarīram āpadaś cāpi vivadanty avihiṃsataḥ kathaṃ yātrā śarīrasya nirārambhasya setsyati
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: For one who does no injury, the body and its distresses are at strife; how shall the body's sustenance be secured for one who undertakes nothing?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca yathā śarīraṃ na glāyen neyān mṛtyuvaśaṃ yathā tathā karmasu varteta samartho dharmam ācaret
english: Bhīṣma said: So that the body does not waste away, so that it does not fall under the sway of death, in such measure should one engage in works; the able man should practise dharma so.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ kāryaṃ parīkṣeta śīghraṃ vātha cireṇa vā sarvathā kāryadurge 'smin bhavān naḥ paramo guruḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How should one examine a deed to be done — swiftly, or with long deliberation? In this stronghold of hard choices you are in every way our highest teacher.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam cirakāres tu yat pūrvaṃ vṛttam āṅgirase kule
english: Bhīṣma said: On this point too they tell this ancient tale of what befell long ago to Cirakārin in the line of Aṅgiras.

sanskrit: cirakārika bhadraṃ te bhadraṃ te cirakārika cirakārī hi medhāvī nāparādhyati karmasu
english: O Cirakārin, blessings on you, blessings on you, O Cirakārin! For the man who acts deliberately is wise, and offends not in his deeds.

sanskrit: cirakārī mahāprājño gautamasyābhavat sutaḥ ciraṃ hi sarvakāryāṇi samekṣāvān prapadyate
english: Cirakārin, the greatly wise, was the son of Gautama; for he undertook all his tasks long and with careful regard.

sanskrit: ciraṃ saṃcintayann arthāṃś ciraṃ jāgrac ciraṃ svapan cirakāryābhisaṃpatteś cirakārī tathocyate
english: Long pondering his aims, long waking, long sleeping, because he carried out his tasks only after long delay, he was therefore called Cirakārin, 'the Slow-Doer.'

sanskrit: alasagrahaṇaṃ prāpto durmedhāvī tathocyate buddhilāghavayuktena janenādīrghadarśinā
english: He earned the name of sluggard and was called dull-witted by people of nimble but shallow understanding, who see not far ahead.

sanskrit: vyabhicāre tu kasmiṃś cid vyatikramyāparān sutān pitroktaḥ kupitenātha jahīmāṃ jananīm iti
english: Now, upon some transgression, passing over his other sons, he was bidden by his enraged father: "Slay this mother of yours!"

sanskrit: sa tatheti cireṇoktvā svabhāvāc cirakārikaḥ vimṛśya cirakāritvāc cintayām āsa vai ciram
english: Having slowly answered "So be it," by his very nature the Slow-Doer, reflecting in his deliberate way, fell long to pondering.

sanskrit: pitur ājñāṃ kathaṃ kuryāṃ na hanyāṃ mātaraṃ katham kathaṃ dharmacchale nāsmin nimajjeyam asādhuvat
english: How shall I carry out my father's command, and how shall I not slay my mother? How shall I keep from sinking, like a wicked man, into this snare disguised as dharma?

sanskrit: pitur ājñā paro dharmaḥ svadharmo mātṛrakṣaṇam asvatantraṃ ca putratvaṃ kiṃ nu māṃ nātra pīḍayet
english: A father's command is the highest dharma; yet a son's own duty is the protection of his mother, and sonship is bound and not its own master — how should this not torment me?

sanskrit: striyaṃ hatvā mātaraṃ ca ko hi jātu sukhī bhavet pitaraṃ cāpy avajñāya kaḥ pratiṣṭhām avāpnuyāt
english: Who, having slain a woman, and his mother at that, could ever know happiness? And who, by slighting his father, could ever win a firm standing?

sanskrit: anavajñā pitur yuktā dhāraṇaṃ mātṛrakṣaṇam yuktakṣamāv ubhāv etau nātivartetamāṃ katham
english: Not to slight the father is fitting; to uphold and protect the mother is fitting too. Both these claims deserve forbearance — how shall I overstep either of them?

sanskrit: pitā hy ātmānam ādhatte jāyāyāṃ jajñiyām iti śīlacāritragotrasya dhāraṇārthaṃ kulasya ca
english: For the father places his own self within the wife, that a child be born, for the sustaining of character, conduct, lineage, and family.

sanskrit: so 'ham ātmā svayaṃ pitrā putratve prakṛtaḥ punaḥ vijñānaṃ me kathaṃ na syād bubudhe cātmasaṃbhavam
english: I myself am that very self, brought forth again by my father into the state of a son; how then should I lack understanding? — and so he came to know his own origin.

sanskrit: jātakarmaṇi yat prāha pitā yac copakarmaṇi paryāptaḥ sa dṛḍhīkāraḥ pitur gauravaniścaye
english: What the father pronounces at the birth-rite and at the rite of initiation — that firm confirmation suffices to establish the reverence due to the father.

sanskrit: gurur agryaḥ paro dharmaḥ poṣaṇādhyayanād dhitaḥ pitā yad āha dharmaḥ sa vedeṣv api suniścitaḥ
english: The father is the foremost teacher, the highest dharma, a benefactor through nurture and the gift of learning; whatever the father declares is dharma, and that too is firmly settled in the Vedas.

sanskrit: prītimātraṃ pituḥ putraḥ sarvaṃ putrasya vai pitā śarīrādīni deyāni pitā tv ekaḥ prayacchati
english: A son is to his father but a source of joy, whereas the father is everything to the son; all things — body and the rest, the gifts that are to be given — the father alone bestows.

sanskrit: tasmāt pitur vacaḥ kāryaṃ na vicāryaṃ kathaṃ cana pātakāny api pūyante pitur vacanakāriṇaḥ
english: Therefore the father's word must be done, and in no way questioned; even his sins are cleansed away for the man who carries out his father's word.

sanskrit: bhoge bhāgye prasavane sarvalokanidarśane bhartrā caiva samāyoge sīmantonnayane tathā
english: In enjoyment, in fortune, in childbearing, in the witness of all the world, in union with a husband, and in the parting of the bride's hair —

sanskrit: pitā svargaḥ pitā dharmaḥ pitā paramakaṃ tapaḥ pitari prītim āpanne sarvāḥ prīyanti devatāḥ
english: The father is heaven, the father is dharma, the father is the highest austerity; when the father is brought to delight, all the gods are delighted.

sanskrit: āśiṣas tā bhajanty enaṃ puruṣaṃ prāha yāḥ pitā niṣkṛtiḥ sarvapāpānāṃ pitā yad abhinandati
english: Whatever blessings the father pronounces, those come to that man; the father is the expiation of all sins, in whatever he gives his glad approval.

sanskrit: mucyate bandhanāt puṣpaṃ phalaṃ vṛntāt pramucyate kliśyann api sutasnehaiḥ pitā snehaṃ na muñcati
english: The blossom is loosed from its stalk, the fruit is loosed from its stem; but the father, though wearied by his love for his sons, never lets his love go.

sanskrit: etad vicintitaṃ tāvat putrasya pitṛgauravam pitā hy alpataraṃ sthānaṃ cintayiṣyāmi mātaram
english: Thus far has the son's reverence for the father been pondered; but the father is the lesser station — now I shall reflect upon the mother.

sanskrit: yo hy ayaṃ mayi saṃghāto martyatve pāñcabhautikaḥ asya me jananī hetuḥ pāvakasya yathāraṇiḥ mātā dehāraṇiḥ puṃsāṃ sarvasyārtasya nirvṛtiḥ
english: This frame of mine, formed of the five elements in mortal life — of it my mother is the cause, as the fire-stick is of the fire; the mother is the kindling-block of men's bodies, the soothing of all who suffer.

sanskrit: na ca śocati nāpy enaṃ sthāviryam apakarṣati śriyā hīno 'pi yo gehe ambeti pratipadyate
english: He grieves not, nor does old age drag him down, who, even bereft of fortune, comes home and finds one to call 'Mother.'

sanskrit: putrapautrasamākīrṇo jananīṃ yaḥ samāśritaḥ api varṣaśatasyānte sa dvihāyanavac caret
english: He who, surrounded by sons and grandsons, still takes refuge with his mother, moves about like a child of two years even at the close of a hundred years.

sanskrit: samarthaṃ vāsamarthaṃ vā kṛśaṃ vāpy akṛśaṃ tathā rakṣaty eva sutaṃ mātā nānyaḥ poṣṭā vidhānataḥ
english: Able or unable, lean or full of flesh — the mother guards her son all the same; no other is his sustainer by ordained right.

sanskrit: tadā sa vṛddho bhavati yadā bhavati duḥkhitaḥ tadā śūnyaṃ jagat tasya yadā mātrā viyujyate
english: Then a man grows old when he grows sorrowful; then the world becomes empty for him, when he is parted from his mother.

sanskrit: nāsti mātṛsamā chāyā nāsti mātṛsamā gatiḥ nāsti mātṛsamaṃ trāṇaṃ nāsti mātṛsamā prapā
english: There is no shade like a mother's, no refuge like a mother's, no protection like a mother's, no fountain of comfort like a mother's.

sanskrit: kukṣisaṃdhāraṇād dhātrī jananāj jananī smṛtā aṅgānāṃ vardhanād ambā vīrasūtvena vīrasūḥ
english: For bearing him in her womb she is the sustainer; for giving him birth she is called the mother; for the nourishing of his limbs she is 'Ambā'; and for bringing forth a hero she is the hero's mother.

sanskrit: śiśoḥ śuśrūṣaṇāc chuśrūr mātā deham anantaram cetanāvān naro hanyād yasya nāsuṣiraṃ śiraḥ
english: For tending the infant she is 'Śuśrū'; the mother is the body's own nearest source. The man of sense would slay her only if his head were no hollow vessel — that is, if he had lost all reason.

sanskrit: dampatyoḥ prāṇasaṃśleṣe yo 'bhisaṃdhiḥ kṛtaḥ kila taṃ mātā vā pitā veda bhūtārtho mātari sthitaḥ
english: What compact was made in the joining of the husband's and wife's life-breath, that the mother knows, or the father; but the truth of the matter rests with the mother.
